html:
The Serbian campaign of World War I began in August 1914, when Austria Hungary invaded Serbia after the Sarajevo assassination, and ended with Serbia's return in 1918.

Serbia beat back the first invasions, winning at Cer in August and at Kolubara in December 1914, the first Allied victories of the war. In late 1915 Germany, Austria and Bulgaria attacked together. The Serbian army, the king and many civilians retreated over the Albanian mountains in winter, and tens of thousands died before the survivors were taken to Corfu. They returned through the Salonika front in 1918. Serbia lost a large share of its population to battle, typhus and hunger, a loss that shaped its place in the new Yugoslav kingdom.
sum: The Serbian campaign of World War I began in August 1914, when Austria Hungary invaded Serbia after the Sarajevo assassination, and ended with Serbia's return in 1918.
